mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI increases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 3 months indicates weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of periods following a sustained decline in HOUST, or the correlation between HOUST declines and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a supply shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO drops and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy in low growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not show a statistically significant correlation with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real final sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not show a statistically significant correlation with positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of economic expansion, a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
